claims.text: As-deposited sputtered non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films have a relatively coarse microstructure.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films exhibit a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
Rapid thermal annealing near 600°C for about 120 seconds is an applicable intervention for the sputtered FeMnNiGeSi films.
Rapid thermal annealing induces nanostructured microdomains in FeMnNiGeSi films.
Rapid thermal annealing refines the grains and increases grain-boundary area in FeMnNiGeSi films.
Rapid thermal annealing promotes crystallization of sputtered films.
The annealing-induced reduction in grain size diminishes energy barriers for magnetic-domain-wall motion.
The annealing-induced microstructure reduces domain-wall pinning.
Reduced domain-wall pinning smooths the magnetostructural transition.
A smoother magnetostructural transition lowers magnetic hysteresis during low-field cooling cycles.
RTA-treated films will have a broader and more continuous magnetostructural transition than as-deposited films.
RTA-treated films will have a significantly smaller low-field hysteresis-loop area than as-deposited films.
RTA treatment may make the entropy-change peak less abrupt.
A less abrupt entropy-change peak facilitates faster heat exchange during magnetic-cooling cycles.
Annealing-induced structural reconfiguration enhances effective surface area for heat exchange.
The predicted behavior applies to sputtered films from tens to a few hundred nanometers thick.
Annealing substantially above the proposed temperature may cause grain growth or secondary effects that negate the benefits.
The RTA treatment can retain the films' mechanical stability.

contradictions.description: The baseline attributes limited heat exchange to a lower surface-to-volume ratio, while the intervention retains comparable thin-film dimensions and the mechanism nevertheless claims an enhanced effective surface area without specifying porosity, roughening, or another geometrical change.

The initial film is described as already having a coarse microstructure and a magnetostructural transition, whereas the proposed mediator is said to arise through rapid crystallization. The hypothesis does not clarify whether the initial film is amorphous, partially crystalline, or coarse-grained crystalline, making the crystallization-to-grain-refinement sequence internally ambiguous.
